issues.description: The return type of getAllPersons() differs between repositories: the template's PersonResource and the PersonService methods use List<Person>, but the solution's PersonResource declares ResponseEntity<java.util.Set<Person>> and returns personService.getAll() (which is a List). This mismatch is a structural type inconsistency that will cause compilation errors or confusion about the intended collection type for the API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent. Either change the solution's PersonResource signature to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> (matching PersonService.getAll()), or change PersonService.getAll() to return a Set<Person> and adapt repository/service implementation accordingly. Preferably, revert PersonResource in the solution to ResponseEntity<List<Person>> to match the template and service implementation.

issues.description: The REST endpoint method getAllPersons is declared to return a List<Person> in the template (and is described in the problem context as returning all persons), but in the solution PersonResource the method signature returns a Set<Person>. Meanwhile, PersonService.getAll() returns a List<Person> in both template and solution. This inconsistent use of collection type names (List vs Set) for the same conceptual operation (returning all persons) creates a naming/type mismatch across artifacts and may confuse students when mapping the problem description to the template and the provided solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a consistent collection type name for the 'get all persons' operation across all artifacts. Either change the solution's PersonResource.getAllPersons signature to ResponseEntity<List<Person>> to match PersonService.getAll(), or change PersonService.getAll() (and the template) to return a Set<Person> and update the problem statement accordingly so all three artifacts use the same identifier/type.
